value: destroy his armour by offensive action, lending weight to the AT layout
armourInDefence.src: Operations of War Vol I (Defence) s6 para 1 p 22
armourInDefence.note: Employed concentrated, the main element of the reserve; within the main defences only in exceptional circumstances (a serious armour threat on an approach with no effective AT obstacle). Vol I (read unlocked 19 Nov 2026) prints no frontage or depth for an armour unit holding ground, so an Armr Regt or Tk Sqn is not offered as the unit of a defence layout: armour joins a Bn defence as its tank Sqns (the C Pen force, AT weight).

armourInAttack.src: Operations of War Vol II (Offensive Operations) s7 paras 20-22 pp 28-29; s5 p 53; Fig 2 p 9
armourInAttack.note: Read unlocked 19 Nov 2026. Groups armour or infantry heavy, or balanced, by terrain, enemy and force; armour heavy attack in semi desert and desert (open spaces), with a favourable air situation; infantry heavy where the ground disallows armour. After a break-out the Armd Div advances on a broad front with two Bdes, each with two Regt groups up or one. No frontage or depth is printed for an armour unit in the attack: frontages 'depend on defender's dispositions and lie of terrain', narrower by night (s9 para 2c p 37), and the attack's distances 'depend upon the terrain and en strength' (Fig 7). Fig 2 (an Armd Bde leading an Armd Div's advance) is a march layout: covering troops 4-8 km ahead, Van Gd about 3500 m, flank guards about 6 km out, the main body about 8 km behind (15-20 km for the Armd Div); the scan is highlighted over in places, so these are read as uncertain.

tankCoverMinM.note: How far beyond the FDL along an approach a tank unit's guns, from its C Pen or Sup posn, must reach for the approach to count as covered by them.

rows: Recoilless rifle back blast danger zone

advance.note: Advance to contact, an Armd Bde leading an Armd Div's advance (OoW Vol II s4 paras 1-5 pp 9-11, Fig 2 p 9). Echelons: covering troops (mobile troops: a Recce Regt and / or a LAT Bn) 4-8 km ahead; the Advance Guard (an Armr Regt group or an Inf Bn group: Van Gd 3500 m, Main Gd 3000 m); the Main Body straight behind it, 6 km deep; the Armd Div's flank guards 15-20 km out; the follow-up Bde up to 8 km behind the leading Bde. The scan is highlighted over; the figures were read from the page's text layer under the highlights and placed by where they stand on the page (19 Nov 2026).

mainBodyBackM.note: The Main Body's head straight behind the Advance Guard: the Van Gd 3500 m and the Main Gd 3000 m.

axisNogoWarn.note: Accepted by the user 19 Nov 2026 with the stretch limits. The share of the axis NO-GO for tracks (the bundle's tracked going, 100 m steps) above which Going on the axis warns.

axisDetourWarn.note: Set by the user 19 Nov 2026 (kept at 1.5). The routed axis against the straight line from the Main Body to the covering troops: longer than this many times, Axis route warns (the ground forces a long way round).

rlApartM.note: The default; the user sets it for each plan in the tab (RL apart: 1, 2 or 3 km; the user, 19 Nov 2026). Report lines are set on the water features across the axis ahead of the SP (canals, distributaries, streams; a report line is usually a terrain feature across the zone: OoW Vol II glossary), at least this far apart, up to four.

axisNogoRunM.note: Set by the user 19 Nov 2026 (kept at 200 / 500 m). The longest NO-GO stretch on the axis: over the first it warns (a bridge or a detour), over the second it fails (the axis is blocked).

airAslt.note: The Air Aslt Bn lifted by the Air Aslt Sqn (PlanAvn). The ORBAT gives the Sqn (p 703: 2 Air Aslt Flts x 6 Air Aslt Hels, a Cargo Sp Flt of 5 Cargo Hels), the types by role (pp 706-708: the Bell 412 the only Air Aslt type; Cargo: Bell 412, Puma, Mi-17, not tied to a Sqn) and their loads and speeds (pp 707-708, 714). The distance, the time on the ground and the build-up allowed are not printed: E until set.

pzLzKm.note: Pick-up zone to landing zone, one way. The plan does not draw the PZ: change it here for the mission.

groundMin.note: Each hel's time on the ground a round trip: loading at the PZ, landing and off-loading at the LZ.

buildUpMaxH.note: The longest the Bn may take to be complete on the LZ after its first wave lands, before he can react in strength.

cargoHel.note: The Cargo Sp Flt's type, not fixed by the book: the Bell 412 (9 troops) is taken; a Puma carries 16, an Mi-17 24 (p 707).

ad.note: AD over a plan's vulnerable points (PlanAD). The ORBAT (SO's Hbk 2019 Sec 3 pp 300-321) gives the units, their fire units and the weapons' max eff slant range (p 317); how they are sited round a VP is not printed there, so these figures are E until set.

releaseM.note: How far out from a VP a fire unit must engage for the VP to count as covered by it: an attacking aircraft or helicopter is to be engaged before it releases (bombs, rockets, ATGMs). Covered: slant range minus the distance FU-to-VP at least this.

minFus.note: Fire units wanted over each VP of the first priority (bridges, gun areas): two, so that one in action or out of it leaves cover.

siteM.note: How far from the VP's centre a fire unit is sited: a quarter of its slant range, held to this band; toward the threat first (forward left, forward right), then behind and on the flanks.

samAssumed.note: The SAM Launcher of the Lt AD Msl Tps and SAM Btys is not named in the charts (pp 308-309): taken as the Anza Mk II (5 km, p 317), the national MANPADS.

checkBands.note: Bands the Check step uses for a pass. E figures are proposals until the user sets them.

fieldOfFireToObstacleM.note: Forward posn to the obstacle or killing ground in front: inside the MG's reach but not on top of it.

gapMaxM.note: Widest gap between forward posns before it needs mines, fire and patrols to close it (doctrine gap 500 m Bn two up, 300 m Pl).

bofFlankMinDeg.note: The BOF fires from a flank: at least 30 degrees off the axis of the assault, so the assault does not mask it.

loeBeyondObjM.note: Limit of exploitation about 600 m beyond the objective's far edge, inside the Bn mortars' cover.

reserveToObjMin.note: Reserve Coy to the objective inside an hour on foot.

assyAccessM.note: A road or track within this of the Assy Area gives the vehicles entry and exit.

assyPreferM.note: The Assy Area further back than this where hidden ground allows.

bofFromObjM.note: BOF sites tried this far from the Obj's centre (and 250 m further): inside the 106 mm RR's reach of its near edge, clear of the assault.

bofOutsideObjM.note: The BOF at least this far outside the Obj's edge: a 1500 m wide Coy locality would otherwise take the nearer sites inside it (seen 15 Nov 2026 on a flank attack).

fupSearchDeg.note: The FUP finder swings this far either way round the Obj (and 100 m in or out) for dead ground.

fupMin.note: Time to form up in the FUP.

spareFactor.note: Added to the approach march for checks, drift and closing up.

msrChoke.src: User, 14 Nov 2026: a flanking attack that chokes the en MSR is encouraged

stepM.note: Searched every 30 m (the bundle grid): a bridge is a cell or two wide.

msrChoke.note: His MSR behind the Obj: a bridge on it first, else a metalled road, between 300 m and 3 km beyond the Obj; the layout whose LOE ends nearest it chokes it.

compareWeights.note: Left against right (frontal for reference): weighed factors, each with its reason; for the user to set. phase2 counts only in a two-phase attack.

tanks.src: IBB S44 para 16 a pp 213-216 (night attack: his ATGMs reach 1500-3500 m and stand 500-1000 m deep, so the tank FUP is 2500-3000 m out and a common FUP with the infantry is no longer feasible; tanks in the fire support role, option a: to the base of fire as the assaulting infantry come as close to the Obj, option b: 1500-3000 m out in open country; night firing range 800 m with NVD, 1600 m effective with registration; hull down and covered approaches; tank noise; tanks within the infantry's protection against tank-hunting parties); S42 pp 181, 186-188 (separate FUPs; the same or converging axes, all converging on the Obj, arriving together; the leading troops shoot the infantry on, then rush the Obj from the infantry's assault line 150/250 m out, arriving just before or with them; the rear troops cover them by observed fire, on the flanks in close country); S35 para 7 b pp 144-146 (open tank country: the tanks lead; fields of fire and observation 400-500 m or less: the infantry leads; 100-200 m or less: the infantry, a troop of tanks at most, the Sqn less a troop following)
tanks.note: None: no tanks with the Bn. Fire sp (infantry heavy): the Sqn waits at FUP (Tks), moves to fire positions by the BOF to arrive as the infantry come as close, and shoots them on. Close sp (armour heavy): the Sqn less a troop from FUP (Tks) on its own axis converging on the Obj, timed to reach the infantry's assault line with them and rush the Obj; a troop covers from a flank.

fupAsideM.note: FUP (Tks) laid this far aside of the infantry's axis, away from the BOF: a place of its own, not the infantry's lane (IBB p181).

fupSearchAsideM.note: The tank FUP finder tries this far either side of the axis, 2500-3000 m out, for ground hidden from the Obj where tracks go.

rushFromM.note: The leading troops rush the Obj when the infantry reach the farther of the two assault line figures.

moveKmh.src: IPB p 18 SLOW-GO vehicle rates (moves.tankKmh): a tactical move bound to bound under fire

aheadMin.note: Close sp: the tanks fire the infantry on from the assault line (IBB p187 b(2)) and rush to be on the Obj this many minutes before them (p187: just before or with them).

nightFireM.src: IBB p214 (T-69 (II) M main gun at night with NVD)

registeredFireM.src: IBB p214 (effective range at night with registration)

rearTroopFromObjM.src: IBB p215 (b) (fire support 1500-3000 m out in open country); p188 c (rear troops cover by observed fire)

whoLeads.note: Fields of fire from the Obj along the approach: beyond openM tanks may lead; openM or less the infantry leads; closeM or less the infantry with a troop at most.

counter.src: IBB p189 paras 22-23 (each Obj organised at once against counter-attack: supporting weapons to pre-designated places, DF adjusted, patrols and OPs out), p191 para 25 (tanks cover likely enemy tank approaches)
counter.note: His counter-attack onto the last objective, read for the reorganisation: his ways in from his depth and how much of each the objective sees.

fromM.note: His counter-attack force waits in his depth: its ways in are sought from this far beyond the last objective, straight behind and 45 degrees either way.

lastStretchM.note: The stretch the reorganised objective must see: inside the 106 mm RR reach, outside the DF safety distances.

deadRunM.note: An unseen stretch this long on a way in (400-1200 m out) is dead ground he can close through: an LP and DF there (IBB p189 d, j).

dfOutM.note: A DF target on each way in this far out (outside the 400-550 m safety distances of field guns and mortars, PlanBuilder_Plan.md 9.1).

phase2.src: IBB s39 p176 c (impetus: the follow-up Coys attack at once when the phase 1 Obj falls; delay gives him time to counter-attack or reorganise), s40 p178 para 6 (objectives and phases, assault and follow-up Coys, a movement and fire plan for each phase), p186 h (follow-up Coys against his flank or rear from a new direction, not passed through the sub-units on the Obj; to exploit success, not to redeem failure; the Bn commits only what the task needs, and tells Bde when all its Coys are committed), p188 para 19, p189 para 23 (each Obj organised at once against counter-attack and as a firm base for the next), p176 d (supporting weapons moved forward as the attack goes on)
phase2.note: Phase 1 is the layout as it stands (frontal, right or left flank) onto Obj 1. The follow-up Coys wait in the FUP, go round Obj 1 once it is taken, form up again at FUP 2 and attack Obj 2 onto its flank; Obj 1 is the firm base that fires for phase 2; the mortars step up to the FUP.

coys.note: The default; the user switches it in the Task step (Ph 2 by) or with R while placing. 2: C and D Coys follow up onto Obj 2 (his depth Coy locality) and no Bn reserve is left: tell Bde (IBB p186 i). 1: C Coy alone, D Coy kept as the Bn reserve (IBB p186 h(3): commit only what the task needs). Either way the BOF is the Spt Coy's weapons (MG, 106 mm RR).

obj2BeyondM.note: Obj 2's centre this far behind Obj 1's when nothing better is known: his depth Coy (a Bn two up is 3-4 km deep, IBB Annex U App 6 p481).

obj2SearchM.note: A hostile unit or posn drawn this far behind Obj 1's centre, within 45 degrees of straight behind, becomes Obj 2; else the highest ground in that band if it stands fit.highGround.gainM higher (his depth on the high ground).

offDeg.note: Phase 2 comes onto Obj 2 this far off the line he faces (a new direction, onto his flank, IBB p186; the same angle as attack.flankDeg). Tried 15 degrees either way on the ground.

fup2FromObj2M.note: FUP 2 beyond the last fire lift plus attack.slBeyondLiftM (600 m) and no further out than the FUP itself (IBB p201: 1000-1200 m).

clearObj1M.note: FUP 2 and the follow-up Coys' way keep this far off Obj 1, so they do not pass through the Coys reorganising on it (IBB p186).

followUpBehindM.src: IBB p204 (7): follow-up Coys 500-750 m behind the forward Coys in the FUP; they move up to the FUP when the assault Coys leave it and stay there until the leading Coys have completed their phase.

waitAt.src: IBB p204 (7) (fup: in the FUP until the leading Coys have completed their phase, 'as ordered'); p186 h(2) (behind: kept close enough to the attacking echelons, as the attack goes on, to press its momentum)
waitAt.note: fup: they leave the FUP for FUP 2 when Obj 1 is taken. behind: they follow the assault from H and wait followUpBehindM short of Obj 1 on their way to FUP 2, so less of the way is left when Obj 1 falls.

morStepUp.src: IBB p176 d (supporting weapons moved forward as soon as possible as the attack goes on)
morStepUp.note: The 81 mm mortars' posn for phase 2: 300 m short of Obj 1's near edge, 500 m to the side away from the phase 2 way, so Obj 2 and the LOE beyond it are in reach (81 mm 3749 m).

fupMin.note: Forming up again at FUP 2; orders and the fire plan switched onto Obj 2 meanwhile (IBB p188 para 19: time for the sub-unit commanders to give orders).

maxGapMin.note: From Obj 1 taken to H2 (crossing SL 2): any longer gives him time to counter-attack or man his depth (IBB p176 c).

layoutHints.basis: E unless a row says otherwise
layoutHints.note: A hint only orders the list Auto tries; the score card decides the ranking.

rows.when: One main approach through a narrow front

rows.why: one Coy on each, the reserve reaching both

rows.when: Wide front, no obstacle, three approaches with tank going
Front on a canal or ditch
rows.src: IBB Annex V App 9 p485 (Bn 2750-4115 m, Coy 1200 m, gap 450 m, mask posns 900-1500 m)

rows.when: Div on an obstacle along the IB
rows.src: Demo2: Bdes three up on the obstacle; Div depth on a D line of planned Bn posns

scoreWeights.src: Judged from what Demo 2 spends its effort on (PlanBuilder_Plan.md 16.4)

restMs.decided: User, 15 Nov 2026: quick ghost while the mouse moves, full fit when it rests

slideMaxM.note: How far a posn may slide out of NO-GO on its own before it is left red.

highGround.decided: User, 15 Nov 2026: a Battle Posn sits near the top of a plateau or on higher ground and may enclose the ITG; the figures are mine.

gainM.note: A posn moves up only when the ground there stands this much higher on average (the 30 m elevation is noisy by a few metres in the plains).

moveM.note: How far a posn moves toward higher ground on its own (J may move it further).

outline.decided: User, 15 Nov 2026: a Battle Posn's outline is curved to suit the ground; the echelon mark stays on its rear side.

scales.note: Each point of the curve may move in or out by up to a quarter of the posn's half-size: out over higher ground, in off NO-GO and water.

perTenthM.note: A point moves a tenth of the way only for 4 m of height gained.

smallOps.note: Phase 8: ambush, patrol and recce in the Intelligent Deployment, laid over the Movement Guide (ambushSites, planPatrol: MovementDoctrine.json) and the Platoon Guide (patrolCard: PlatoonDoctrine.json). Their rules are R (OCOKA_Roadmap.md ch 6: IC / IBB, page to be cited); the figures here are what the Plan Builder adds: how near the click must be to a road, the bands its checks use, the default distances. Mine (E) unless marked.

ambush.src: OCOKA_Roadmap.md ch 6: defile or bend, target hidden from following vehicles, covered withdrawal, away from reinforcements; line, L or V layout; meeting point 750-900 m back (IC / IBB, page to be cited). Layout figures as MovementDoctrine.json ambush (kzM 150, stopM 100, followM 300: E).

rvM.note: The RV (meeting point) 750-900 m back from the ambush along a covered withdrawal.

onRoadM.note: A click this near a road or track lays the KZ on it without a warning.

snapM.note: No road or track this near the click: the KZ is laid across country along the aim, and the check fails.

upM.note: How far up the road (toward where he comes from) the route is read: his column behind the KZ and better sites.

downM.note: How far down the road (beyond the KZ) the route is read.

fireEyeM.note: The fire group kneeling or lying behind cover on 30 m elevation.

vehicleM.note: A soft-skinned vehicle's height, the target.

kzSeen.note: Share of the KZ the fire group sees: under the first fails, under the second warns.

betterBy.note: A site along the road scoring this much more is offered as a better one.

shapePenalty.note: Points off a layout the ground does not suit (Auto ranks the ground's own first).

movers.note: The target: wheeled (the default), tracked, or on foot; its NO-GO decides whether it can leave the road.

outlyingM.note: Area ambush (IC s44 p 152, Fig 16: R): each outlying ambush this far up or down the Rd from the central KZ, beyond the central site's stops and short of his reaction.

outlyingKzM.note: An outlying ambush's own killing stretch (a Sec), read for the share in view.

outlyingMinScore.note: An outlying site scoring under this warns (the same site score as the central one).

outlyingSeenPct.note: An outlying ambush seeing less of its stretch than this warns.

patrol.src: OCOKA_Roadmap.md ch 6 / PlatoonDoctrine.json patrol: legs end on features recognisable at night; bounds 550-750 m apart; final meeting point (FRV) 400-500 m from the objective; night routes avoid wood edges, villages, tracks and skylines; route out differs from route in; 120 paces = 100 m (IC / IBB, page to be cited).

defaultObjM.note: Geometry only, before the objective is aimed at: the Obj this far ahead.

objSizeM.note: The Obj drawn round the aimed point.

seenPct.note: Share of the route out the threat may see: over the first warns, over the second fails.

taskMin.note: Time at the objective in the round trip.

nightH.note: Hours of darkness the round trip is held to (winter longer, summer shorter: set by the user).

maxCells.note: The route grid's size (MovementDoctrine patrol.maxCells 300): kept lower so the fit at rest stays quick.

recce.src: PlanBuilder_Plan.md 9.4: OPs on high ground with sight to the area, routes in dead ground, a recce task list. Figures mine until the user gives the pamphlet's.

defaultAreaM.note: Geometry only, before the area is aimed at: the NAI this far ahead.

naiM.note: The NAI (wide x deep) drawn round the aimed point, square to the line from the base.

opBandM.note: OPs this far from the NAI's centre: out of his small arms, within binocular identification.

opSpreadDeg.note: OPs within this angle either side of the line back to the base (the own side).

opEyeM.note: An observer lying or kneeling in the OP.

opsApartM.note: OPs at least this far apart: one shell, one OP.

seenPct.note: Share of the NAI the OPs see together: under the first fails, under the second warns.

routeSeenPct.note: Share of a route in the NAI may see before it warns.

screen.src: IC s73 pp 378-381, Screens: Coy / Pl / Sec outposts laid laterally with intervals in front or on the exposed flanks of the main posn; only as far forward as is necessary to deny him observation and recce of the main posn and its obstacles; on his likely approaches, on defensible ground with clear observation and covered routes of withdrawal (p 378); strength by the frontage screened, the time, the threat and the ground (p 379); mines in front and on the flanks (p 380); sections not split, alternative fire trenches (p 380); withdrawal along a covered route on the order of the commander who ordered it, or on 50 % casualties / the time up if comms break (p 381). Figures below E unless marked.

frontM.note: The frontage of the defence screened (IC p379 a): a Bn front, laid across the aim.

fwdM.note: How far forward of the main posn the posts go; IC p378 gives an isolated knoll about 600 m from the FDLs as an example.

defaultWatchM.note: Geometry only, before the aim: the ground in front this far out.

watchDepthM.note: The depth of the ground in front read (where he would watch the main posn from).

postsApartM.note: Posts at least this far apart (laterally with intervals).

spanShare.note: The posts span at least this share of the front, else bunched.

stepM.note: The grid the posts are searched on.

postEyeM.note: A post's eye: lying or kneeling in a trench on 30 m elevation.

tankEyeM.note: A Recce Sqn's AFV Tp as a post: the commander's eye in the cupola, hull down (no figure in the books read).

hisEyeM.note: His observer in the ground in front.

mainTallM.note: What he looks for in the main posn (trenches, wire, vehicles).

seenPct.note: Share of the ground he would watch from that the posts see: under the first fails, under the second warns.

routeSeenPct.note: A way back more in his view than this warns.

postKinds.note: Features tried as posts (the knoll of IC p378).

nearPts.note: Points a post at the near edge of the band scores over one at the far edge (only as far forward as is necessary: IC p378).

crossing.note: Phase 7: an assault across a water obstacle and the bridgehead (PlanCrossing.ts over the Movement Guide's Water engine, MovementDoctrine.json water). Figures as written in IBB S46-47 (pp 231-262) and Annex Q (pp 467-468), IC s70-71 (pp 355-366), OoW II s14 (pp 49-56); mine marked E.

bdePh1DepthM.note: The first phase ends about 300-600 m ahead of the bund.

bdePh2WidthM.note: Each brigade area on completion of the break-in.

bdeFourBnDepthM.note: With four battalions the brigade phase may go to about 2500 m deep.

bnFrontM.note: The two leading battalions attack on a narrow front each.

bnBreakInWidthM.note: The leading battalions expand sideways to secure this width and 600 m depth.

passThroughDepthM.note: The third battalion passes through and expands the bridgehead to about this depth.

divWidthM.src: IBB S46 para 17 p237, Fig 20; OoW II s14

divDepthM.src: IBB S46 para 17 p237; OoW II s14 p49-56 (8 x 6 km)

divAreaKm2.note: An armoured division group in the bridgehead: 10-12 km2 the break-in infantry division (mostly on the periphery), 18-20 the armoured division, about 10 the follow-in-zone infantry division, AD and engineers.

coyBundM.note: A leading assault company may be given about 300 m of the bund to clear (an enemy platoon holds 275-300 m with 150 m between platoons).

bnPh2WidthM.note: One battalion alone: half of the two leading battalions' 1500-1800 m.

observe.src: IBB S46 para 24 p240; IC s71 para 13 p365: primary objectives are the positions from which he puts aimed small arms fire onto the crossing places; secondary objectives those that overlook the obstacle and direct his artillery onto them.

smallArmsM.note: Aimed small arms fire onto the crossing places: these posns are taken in phase 1.

targetM.note: Men in a boat at the water line.

maxM.note: How far out his observers are looked for.

stepM.note: The grid his observers are looked for on.

driftTimesWidth.note: In flowing water the entry is made upstream to cater for the drift, roughly twice the width of the obstacle.

boat.src: IBB Annex Q para 3 p467: M2 assault boat, paddled by infantry, crew 3, 12 armed men, 10 min a round trip over a 30 m gap; para 1: 48 M2 assault boats with an Inf Div, an Armd Div, Corps engineers

boatsPerBn.note: A leading battalion's share of the division's 48 boats (three leading battalions).

coyMen.note: A rifle company in the boats (8 boats of 12).

bnHqMen.note: Bn HQ and the support weapons' crews that cross by boat.

waveGapMin.note: A and B Coys cross at H hour, C Coy at H+20.

rafts.src: IBB Annex Q para 3 pp 467-468 (construction day / moonlight / dark night, minutes; round trip over a 30 m gap)

bridges.src: IBB Annex Q paras 1-2 p467 (spans held and construction timings in hours: day / moonlight / dark night)

trackwayM.note: Assault track-way Class 30, Corps engineers (Annex Q para 1)

seatsM.note: Added to the water gap for the bridge's seats on both banks.

bridgeLayerMaxM.note: A major enemy obstacle is generally over 80 ft (24 m) wide so that bridge layer tanks cannot bridge it in a rush.

lanesH.note: Engineers start work as soon as possible after H; the lanes are needed after 3-3.5 h.

breach.src: IBB Annex Q para 4 p468: a 108 x 7.2 m lane, one engineer platoon per 108 m of depth; 4 / 5 / 6 h (day / moonlight / dark) without viper, 3 / 4 / 4 with baby viper; infantry 50 %

enemyMinefieldM.src: IBB S47 para 6 p243 (IC s70 para 2a p355: 600-900 m)
enemyMinefieldM.note: Mixed minefields in front of a defended water obstacle.

highFarBankM.note: A far bank this high above the water is scaled with ladders and grapnels (IBB S47; IC s70 para 4f p358).

sqnTanks.note: A tank squadron for the Class 50 raft.

nightH.note: Hours of darkness (night assault preferable: IBB S46 para 18 p237; bridgehead and induction ideally in one night, break-out at first light: OoW II s14).

light.note: Annex Q column the times are taken from: day, moon(light) or dark (night).

bridgeSearchM.note: How far either side of the planned bridge site the ground is read for a better one.

assy.src: IC s71 para 7 pp 362-363, IBB S46 para 8 pp 233-234: concentration area out of enemy artillery range; one Bde Assy Area; a Bn Assy Area per assault Bn not far from the obstacle; boat off-loading point; checkpoint; FUP (when the home bank is secure the water line is the start line); crossing places; vehicle waiting areas near the obstacle, release points on the far bank

placeSearchM.note: How far either side an assault crossing place may move along the bank for a better boat site (it stays on its Coy's front, about 300 m of the bund: IC s70 para 4c p358).

canal.note: Defence on a canal or ditch (the mirror of the crossing): IC s85 pp 449-458 and IBB S57 paras 25-26 pp 316-318, Fig 34. Laid along the obstacle by PlanCrossing.canalPrep, checked by the defence engine (approaches cross it only at its bridges and fords).

bnThreeUpMaxM.note: A battalion with three companies up may cover up to 5000 m.

bnTwoUpFrontM.note: Two companies up on the obstacle, the depth companies and counter penetration posns AA, BB, CC behind.

fdlFromCentreM.note: The forward posns' front edge on the home bank, this far from the water's centre line on a canal of 90 m (moved back as its crest lies further out).

maskAheadM.note: Mask posns for some major weapons ahead of the obstacle (IC s85 para 7 p455), this far beyond the far bank.

mfFarDepthM.note: The minefield on the far side (IC s85 para 17 a p457: ideally on both sides; on the home side only in the gaps).

homeRaiseM.note: Home banks near the border raised 1-2 m astride the major enemy approaches for observation and fields of fire.

rules.text: Defences on the obstacle itself near the border; the bulk on the higher bank, or the far bank if equal; forward elements fall back behind it; depth at Coy / Bn at all costs; no uncommitted reserve at Bn / Coy, depth troops counter-penetrate; reserves not forward of the obstacle; AT weapons in depth when on the home side, some with the mask posns; minefields on both sides, the home side only in the gaps; double concertina both sides; bridges Class 9/12 on tracks, 40/70 on main roads.
